User CSV path with occurrence data. If the CSV file is not in the
current workspace, change to the correct file path
(e.g. “/Users/darwin/Documents/occs/”).

```{r}

# get a list of species occurrence data
userOccs_Oh <- occs_userOccs(
  txtPath = occs_path,
  txtName = "ODOCOILEUS.csv",
  txtSep = ",",
  txtDec = ".")
occs_Oh <- userOccs_Oh$ODOCOILEUS_hemious$cleaned
```

Thanks in advance,

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Error in the result Rmd
parts:
I think the problem might simply be with the line:
occs_path <- ""
You need to enter your file path between the quotation marks. This is setting the path to where the file is located. Control-Click-Option on a Mac or Shift-Right Click on a PC gives the option to "copy as a pathname" which can be pasted.
Example: occs_path <- "Users/YourName/OccRecords/"

Otherwise the issue might be with the definition of the separators and decimals. Check your csv file to make sure that it matches as you have it set (the commas(,) as the separator and periods(.) as the decimals).

Bethany
